title: Envelope
description: The frame every message travels in, on both channels. WebSocket text frames on the agent channel; newline-delimited JSON on the supervisor socket.

agent.description: Panel and agent, over the WebSocket the agent dials to /ws/agent.

supervisor.description: Agent and gss-init, over the unix socket gss-init listens on inside each game container.

PROTOCOL_VERSION.description: Version of this protocol. Sent in `enrol` and `hello`; the panel refuses versions it does not speak with `CLOSE_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`.

MAX_FRAME_BYTES.description: Largest frame either side accepts, in bytes of UTF-8 JSON (one WebSocket text frame, or one NDJSON line on the supervisor socket). Senders split console data well below it (`CONSOLE_BATCH_MAX_BYTES`); a provision spec with hook files is the largest frame.

HELLO_TIMEOUT_SEC.description: Seconds the panel waits for the first frame (`enrol` or `hello`) before closing with `CLOSE_HELLO_TIMEOUT`.

CLOSE_PROTOCOL_ERROR.description: WebSocket close code: a frame was not valid JSON or broke the envelope rules.

CLOSE_UNAUTHORIZED.description: WebSocket close code: the `enrol` token or the `hello` credential was refused (sent after an `unauthorized` response). An agent whose hello was answered `unauthorized` stops reconnecting.

CLOSE_REVOKED.description: WebSocket close code: the host was disabled or removed while connected, or a `hello` was refused because the host is disabled (`forbidden` response). The agent retries slowly; the next `hello` tells a disabled host (keep waiting) from a removed one (`unauthorized`, stop).

CLOSE_HELLO_TIMEOUT.description: WebSocket close code: no `enrol` or `hello` within `HELLO_TIMEOUT_SEC`. Transient: the agent reconnects with its normal backoff.

CLOSE_REPLACED.description: WebSocket close code: a newer connection for the same host took over.

CLOSE_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.description: WebSocket close code: the panel does not speak the agent's `protocolVersion`.

CLOSE_ENROLLED.description: WebSocket close code: enrolment finished; the socket was only for the `enrol` request.

Envelope.description: One frame. Requests carry `id` + `type` + `data`; responses echo `id` and `type` and carry `ok` with `data` or `error`; events carry `type` + `data` and no `id`.

id.description: Correlates a response with its request. Unique per sender for the life of the connection (e.g. `a-17`, `p-17`).

type.description: Message type, e.g. `hello` or `server.start`. Required on requests and events; echoed on responses.

data.description: Payload. Its shape is given by `type` and `kind` (see the message tables).

ok.description: Responses only: whether the request succeeded.

message.description: Readable sentence that tells the operator what to do.

port.description: Set with `port_in_use`: the host port Docker could not bind.

PortInUse.description: A host port something else already holds (M3: Docker's bind failed). The panel retries the allocation once without it.
